question: When you drag a component onto the canvas, should you get the original or a copy?
context: The report was that a component copy shows a wall of authoring controls. It turns out a copy does not: it shows a short panel with the look picker and the values. What happened is that the Button dropped on the canvas was the ORIGINAL, because the first drop of any component is the original and every drop after it is a copy. So this is really a question about what a drag should hand you.

options.label: Always a copy
options.summary: Dragging a Button onto the canvas always puts down a copy. The original goes off to one side, in the same place a second look of a component already lands, so it is there to edit when you want it and never the thing under your pointer. Clicking what you just dropped always gives you the short panel: pick a look, fill in the values.
pros: What you click is always the thing you meant to click
The panel you get never depends on whether you have dropped this component before
Matches what every other design tool does with a library
cons: A drawing you did not ask for appears beside your drop the first time
The original sitting on the canvas can be moved, hidden or deleted by accident
options.mitigation: The original arrives where extra looks already arrive, clear of everything, and its layers row wears the four-diamond mark so it reads as the original at a glance.

options.label: Say it plainly and offer a copy
options.summary: Nothing moves. The first drop is still the original, but its panel says so louder and carries one press, Place a Copy, right under the name. You click the Button you dropped, read that this is the master, press once, and you have the copy you wanted.
pros: Small, and nothing about the canvas changes
Teaches the difference at the moment it matters
The original stays where you put it
cons: You still have to notice and act before you can configure anything
What you get from a drag still depends on invisible history
options.mitigation: The press sits directly under the name, above everything else in the section, so it is the first thing in reach rather than something to go hunting for.

options.label: Originals leave the canvas
options.summary: The canvas only ever holds copies. A component original lives on the Library shelf, and you edit it by opening it in a room of its own rather than by finding it among your drawings. Dragging always gives a copy because there is nothing else it could give.
pros: The canvas is your work, not a mix of your work and your parts bin
One rule with no exception: everything on the canvas is a copy
Editing an original is a deliberate act you cannot stumble into
cons: The biggest change of the three, and it touches how components are made, not just how they are dropped
Losing sight of the original makes comparing looks side by side harder
options.mitigation: The room shows every look of the component beside each other, which is the comparison the canvas was being used for.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.summary: The first drop stays the original and the panel stays as it is. Somebody who wants a copy drags a second one on, or uses Place a Copy on the Library tile.
pros: The original being on the canvas is how looks are edited today
cons: The confusion you hit is still there for the next person, and for you next time
What a drag gives you keeps depending on history nobody can see
options.mitigation: None. This is the behaviour that produced the report.
